trend_source: This US TikTok ('invest in yourself first, you are your greatest asset') pulled 535.1k views and 153.8k likes. The message resonates because people want permission to spend on growth.
title: Your biggest asset isn't in your portfolio, it's you
hooks: The best investment I ever made wasn't a fund, it was a skill that raised my income.
Before you obsess over returns, ask what your own earning power is worth.
You are your greatest asset, so why is that the one thing most people never protect?
talking_points: Your future income is likely the largest asset you'll ever own; upskilling and health compound it
But an asset that big deserves a backup plan if illness or injury stops the paycheck
Income protection and adequate health coverage keep your self-investment from unravelling
Balance: pour into yourself, and put a safety net under that income
cta: Comment ASSET and I'll share a simple way to work out what your income is really worth protecting.
why_it_works: It builds on a hugely shared self-improvement message and honestly extends 'you are your greatest asset' into protecting that asset.
how_to_film: Talk straight to camera, medium shot. Open with the hook in one breath, then a quick beat before pivoting to 'so how do you protect it?'. Keep energy warm, not salesy.
author: @dananozime

trend_source: A 22-year-old US creator broke down five income streams totalling $23,645 for August (852.1k views, 110.8k likes). Viewers love the transparent income-vs-spend format.
title: Multiple income streams look great, until you see how little was kept
hooks: She made $23,000 in a month from five jobs, but here's the number nobody talks about.
Multiple income streams are trendy, keeping the money is the real skill.
Earning more feels amazing until the spending quietly rises to match it.

Track what you keep, not just what you make

why_it_works: It rides a proven transparent-income format while making the honest point that gross income means little without a keeping system.
how_to_film: Show yourself reacting to the idea of 5 income streams, then flip to a whiteboard or on-screen text of the 'pay yourself first' order. Brisk pace.
author: @leila_tuck

author: @yamsterdami

author: @justtonch

trend_source: A US 'get rich the stoic way' video (302.5k views, 21.2k likes) argues wealth comes from discipline and controlling what you can, not chasing everything you see.

Most people worry about the economy and ignore their own $700 monthly commitments.

The stoic investor focuses on repeatable decisions, not predictions
In SG that means automating savings, staying invested through noise, and avoiding lifestyle creep
Wanting less is a legitimate wealth strategy

author: @wealthzipp

author: @the.finance.engineer

trend_source: A phone reel teasing the next foldable/iPhone upgrade went viral at 2.6M views, ~203x the creator's usual. The eternal upgrade itch is universal.

hooks: I almost pre-ordered the new phone too, then I did the maths.

That 'I can't wait for the new one' feeling has a price tag over ten years.
talking_points: Estimate the yearly gap between upgrading annually vs every 3 to 4 years
Redirect the difference into an automated investment each year
You still enjoy tech, just on a cheaper cadence, and the gap compounds
This isn't anti-fun; it's choosing which wants to fund

author: @sethisfy
